items.title: MaskYard
items.text:
Build, store, and inspect chip layouts with Python and KLayout. MaskYard stores cell geometry and hierarchy in a database so you can reuse generated cells and browse their layouts.

Create your first cell · Open the layout viewer · Explore the 30-MZI example

items.title: Hierarchy and ports
items.text:
An instance places a child cell in a parent. Use parent.add_instance(child, name="first", trans=kdb.Trans(200, 0)) to reuse the child geometry with a translation of 200 DBU along x. Each instance can have its own name and transform.

A cell port identifies a connection point and uses a transform to describe its position and orientation. A symmetric cross-section describes the port's width, layer, and enclosure. Ports on an instance reflect the placement of that instance in its parent. Use cell.get_port(name) and cell.get_instance(name) to retrieve named objects.

See batched writes for saving an entire cell hierarchy in one transaction.

items.title: Cells, layers, and geometry
items.text:
A Cell stores a piece of layout. Create it in a database session, use cell.shapes(kdb.LayerInfo(layer, datatype)) to access a layer's shapes, and commit to persist your work. A registered Layer can also be looked up by name through cell.layer(name="metal").

Integer KLayout geometry such as kdb.Box uses database units (DBU). The default DBU is 0.001 µm, so 1,000 integer units represent 1 µm. Use to_dbu and to_um from maskyard.config when moving between integer geometry and micrometres. See database setup before selecting a different DBU.

Cell.write("layout.gds") exports the cell with its descendants. Use an .oas suffix for OASIS.

items.title: PDKs and PCells
items.text:
Use get_or_create_pdk(name) to obtain a named process design kit (PDK) and pdk.pcell() to register a Python function as a parametric cell (PCell) factory. The function takes layout parameters and returns a Cell. Call pdk.create_cell() inside the factory to use its automatically assigned name.

Each PCell factory has a persistent identity. Equivalent normalized arguments can reuse a saved cell across sessions. On the same host, generation locks coordinate identical calls across processes. A database uniqueness constraint prevents duplicate keyed rows, including when processes on different hosts compute the same result.

PCell calls run synchronously by default. See batched writes for writer-backed persistence and Ray for remote tasks.

items.title: Generate a 30-MZI chip
items.text:
The example builds a hierarchy of 30 Mach–Zehnder interferometers in a 5 × 6 array. It uses PCells for reusable geometry and writes a CSV with each device's position and path length difference. The MMI geometry is illustrative and requires foundry validation before fabrication.

Run from the repository root. Keep scratch in the current shell for the viewer command.

scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
export MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///$scratch/chip.db"
uv run --locked python examples/chip_30_mzis.py --output "$scratch/chip.gds"
uv run --locked --extra web uvicorn maskyard.web:app

The script writes chip.gds and chip.csv to the scratch directory. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/, select the saved cell from the chip factory, and use Fit layout to see the whole array.

items.title: How the script adds fill
items.text:
The chip() factory builds the base hierarchy. Running the script calls main(), which uses top.fill() to add 200 nm square fill cells with a 5 µm clearance around the waveguides before exporting the GDS. The guard skips fill generation if the saved chip already contains it.

top = chip()
fill_cell = fill_wg()
if not any(instance.cell_id == fill_cell.id for instance in top.instances):
    top.fill(
        fill_cell,
        fill_regions=[
            (
                kdb.Region(
                    kdb.Box(
                        nm(20),
                        nm(20),
                        nm(CHIP_WIDTH - 20),
                        nm(CHIP_HEIGHT - 20),
                    )
                ),
                0,
            )
        ],
        exclude_layers=[(WG, nm(5))],
        row_step=kdb.Vector(400, 50),
        col_step=kdb.Vector(-50, 400),
        tile_size=(nm(200), nm(200)),
    )
top.write(args.output)

At whole-chip scale, the viewer shows dense fill as a shaded coverage preview. Zoom in beside a waveguide to see the individual squares and the clearance around it.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
MaskYard requires Python 3.14 or later. From a checkout of this repository, use uv to install the project and its locked dependencies.

uv sync --locked

KLayout's Python package is installed as a dependency. To install the browser viewer or Ray support, pass --extra web or --extra ray to uv sync or uv run.

Continue with the quickstart.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
Complete installation, then run this from the repository root in a Bash-compatible shell. The script runs in a scratch directory and uses a fresh SQLite database.

repo="$PWD"
scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
(
  cd "$scratch"
  MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///$scratch/quickstart.db" \
    uv run --project "$repo" --locked python "$repo/docs/examples/quickstart.py"
)
printf 'Outputs are in %s\n' "$scratch"

items.title: Create, save, and export
items.text:
The script inserts a box on layer 1, datatype 0, commits the cell, and loads it by ID in a new session. It exports first_cell.gds and reopens the file with KLayout's Python API. With the default database unit of 0.001 µm, the box is 10 × 5 µm.

from maskyard import Cell, kdb
from maskyard.engine import session_context
from maskyard.models.cell import create_cell

with session_context() as session:
    cell = create_cell("first_cell")
    cell.shapes(kdb.LayerInfo(1, 0)).insert(kdb.Box(0, 0, 10_000, 5_000))
    session.commit()
    cell_id = cell.id

with session_context() as session:
    saved_cell = session.get(Cell, cell_id)
    assert saved_cell is not None
    saved_cell.write("first_cell.gds")

layout = kdb.Layout()
layout.read("first_cell.gds")
assert layout.cell("first_cell").bbox() == kdb.Box(0, 0, 10_000, 5_000)
print(f"Saved cell {cell_id} and exported first_cell.gds")

Open the GDS in KLayout, or use the layout viewer with the same database.

items.title: Batch cell writes
items.text:
Build detached cells with persist=False and submit them to the dedicated writer. submit_cell snapshots the cell on the calling thread and returns a Future[int] that resolves to the saved cell ID after commit.

from maskyard import kdb, shutdown_writer, submit_cell
from maskyard.models.cell import create_cell

cell = create_cell("leaf", persist=False)
cell.shapes(kdb.LayerInfo(1, 0)).insert(kdb.Box(0, 0, 100, 100))

try:
    pending_id = submit_cell(cell)
    print(pending_id.result())
finally:
    shutdown_writer()

Use add_instance(child) and attach_port(name, cross_section) to assemble the graph before submission. New children save in the parent's transaction. You can also load an existing child by ID and attach it. Ports require a saved cross-section.

The writer commits up to 64 requests per transaction or collects requests for up to 5 ms after the first. If one request fails, the batch rolls back and its futures raise. Set flush=True to skip the batching delay when the next cell depends on this write. Call shutdown_writer() to drain the queue.

For a PCell factory, use @pdk.pcell(use_writer=True) and return a cell built with pdk.create_cell(persist=False). The decorated call waits for its saved cell before returning.

items.title: Configure the database
items.text:
MaskYard defaults to sqlite:///maskyard.db in the current directory. Set MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL before importing MaskYard or starting the viewer. Use an absolute SQLite URL to share the same file across processes started from different directories.

export MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:////absolute/path/to/layout.db"

Use maskyard.engine.session_context() to open a session and call session.commit() after changes you want to persist. A new database defaults to 0.001 µm per DBU. To initialize a fresh database with a different unit, call create_db_and_tables(dbu=...) before any other database access.

When an existing database's schema or DBU is incompatible, initialization can drop and recreate its tables. Export layouts you want to preserve and use a new database file when changing DBU.

items.title: Run PCells with Ray
items.text:
From the repository root, install the optional Ray dependency and run the example with a fresh SQLite database. The driver and workers must share the same absolute database path.

scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///$scratch/ray.db" \
  uv run --locked --extra ray python docs/examples/ray_pcell.py

import ray

from maskyard import Cell, get_or_create_pdk, kdb

pdk = get_or_create_pdk("ray_example")


@pdk.pcell(ray=True)
def rectangle(width: int) -> Cell:
    """Build a rectangle 100 database units tall using the supplied width."""
    cell = get_or_create_pdk("ray_example").create_cell()
    cell.shapes(kdb.LayerInfo(1, 0)).insert(kdb.Box(0, 0, width, 100))
    return cell


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ray.init(num_cpus=2, include_dashboard=False)
    try:
        ref = rectangle.remote(200)
        print(rectangle.get_cell(ref).id)
    finally:
        ray.shutdown()

With @pdk.pcell(ray=True), .remote(...) returns an ObjectRef[int] for the saved cell ID. Equivalent calls in one process reuse the same reference. .get_cell(ref) waits for the task and loads the result in the caller's session. Pass plain parameters to tasks and keep ORM objects and sessions in their owning processes.

items.title: Open the layout viewer
items.text:
Use the same SQLite file as your layout generation script. From the repository root, replace the path below with the absolute path of that database.

MASKYARD_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////absolute/path/to/layout.db \
  uv run --locked --extra web uvicorn maskyard.web:app

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and select a cell. The cell page shows its hierarchy and layout. Use Fit layout, the grid control, and the layer toggles to inspect the geometry. Try the 30-MZI example for a hierarchy with multiple layers.

The web app serves bundled assets and generates compressed geometry chunks as needed. SQLite writes invalidate cached cells on their next request. Set MASKYARD_LAYOUT_CACHE_DIR to choose the output directory, or warm the cache with uv run --locked --extra web maskyard-build-render-cache using the same database environment.

Set MASKYARD_LAYOUT_LAYER_PROPERTIES to a KLayout .lyp file to customize layer colors, visibility, outlines, and fills. Unmatched layers retain the default styles. Built-in stipples beyond solid and hollow use a default pattern. Reload the viewer after editing the file.
